verdict.rationale: Klaviyo documents natural-language operation in two ways. In-app, Composer lets you "tell Composer what you're trying to achieve" and it builds the audience, drafts content, plans the send and can make supported changes. Headlessly, the official MCP server lets agents like Claude or Cursor act on prompts such as "Create an email campaign promoting our Memorial Day sale," covering tasks from campaign creation to flow reports. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that these natural-language commands work as claimed, and clear documentation of which actions Composer supports versus which still need the UI.
